bentoItems.title: Find Your Instrument
bentoItems.subtitle: Master Luthier Bench Setup
bentoItems.description: Discover master-crafted violins, violas, cellos, and basses. While corporate chains ship factory-pressed plywood in cardboard boxes, every instrument at our independent Louisville shop is personally inspected, carved, and acoustically tuned by hand for rich, effortless projection.

bentoItems.title: Strings & Cases
bentoItems.subtitle: Concert Protection
bentoItems.description: Protect and optimize your voice. Hand-selected luxury suspension cases, Pirastro, Larsen, and Thomastik-Infeld strings, and bespoke carved tonewood fittings.

bentoItems.title: Student Rentals
bentoItems.subtitle: The 100% Equity Promise
bentoItems.description: We reject the disposable rental racket. Area students receive genuine, shop-graduated tonewood instruments with all setup work done in-house. 100% of first-year rental equity applies toward owning a master instrument.

bentoItems.title: The Guarantee
bentoItems.subtitle: The Craftsman's Guarantee · 100% Equity
bentoItems.description: The big-box conglomerates profit off student depreciation. We stake our livelihood on your growth: 100% of your investment follows you forever when you step up to your next master instrument.

bentoItems.title: Restoration & Repair
bentoItems.subtitle: Purist Benchwork · Since 1976
bentoItems.description: No factory assembly lines. No outsourced regional depots. Complete restoration, precision soundpost adjustment, and acoustic bench setup executed directly by Matthew Lane at our Wallace Ave workbench.

bentoItems.title: Bow Services
bentoItems.subtitle: Master Rehairs & Balance
bentoItems.description: Precision bow rehairs using select unbleached Mongolian stallion hair. Hand-tied, individually combed, and balanced for lightning bite, seamless string crossing, and acoustic clarity.

bentoItems.title: Private Instruction
bentoItems.subtitle: The Oral Tradition
bentoItems.description: Connect with Louisville's foremost pedagogues, concertmasters, and Suzuki specialists. Mentoring young artists from their first posture to youth orchestra auditions and conservatory stages.

bentoItems.title: Our Story
bentoItems.subtitle: Two Generations · One Unbroken Line
bentoItems.description: Founded by Mark Edwards (1952-2026), our shop was built on fifty years of pure devotion to tone. Fit for his first violin here as a young boy in 1988, Matthew Lane worked twenty years at Mark's bench. Today, Matt holds the line: an independent luthier whose hand-carved plates and acoustic truth prove that real craftsmanship outlives every corporate trend.

bentoItems.title: Visit Us
bentoItems.subtitle: Historic St. Matthews · Louisville, KY
bentoItems.description: Located at 315 Wallace Ave, Louisville, KY 40207. Step into the scent of seasoned spruce, maple shavings, and rosin. Book an in-person acoustic audition or consult directly with Matthew Lane.

story.headline: The Craft That Refused to Yield
story.subtitle: How a boy fitted for a rental in 1988 grew into a master luthier who held his ground when conglomerates circled—preserving what automated factories can never replicate: acoustic truth.
story.benchSubtitle: Hand-graduating plate thickness to 0.1mm acoustic tolerance
paragraphs: In 1988, a nine-year-old boy stepped into Mark Edwards Violins on Wallace Avenue. Mark carefully fitted him for his very first rental violin. That boy was Matthew Lane.

Most students eventually set their instruments down. Matt never did. In 2005, he returned to the shop not as a customer, but as Mark's dedicated apprentice. For over two decades, the two worked shoulder-to-shoulder, preserving the exact hand-carving, varnishing, and acoustic arching disciplines handed down through Cremona and Paris.

When Mark Edwards passed in early 2026, corporate music chains and private-equity retail aggregators circled with acquisition offers. Matt refused every inquiry. Instead, he renewed the craftsman's sacred promise: every violin, viola, and cello that leaves this door will be personally tuned and set up by hand, backed by 100% lifetime equity, and built with an integrity no assembly line could ever buy.

tenet1.title: The Hand vs. The 10,000-Box Factory
tenet1.text: Corporate distributors order shipping containers of mass-pressed plywood instruments drowned in thick polyurethane that suffocates resonance. At Lane & Edwards, every bridge is carved by hand, every soundpost is positioned to 0.1mm, and every spruce plate is graduated with micro finger planes until the wood breathes like a cathedral.

tenet2.title: The 100% Equity Shield
tenet2.text: The mass-retail model thrives on planned obsolescence and steep depreciation—where families lose 80% of their investment on disposable student instruments. At Lane & Edwards, 100% of your rental and instrument payments transfer directly toward future master acquisitions. We protect your family's musical journey for life.

tenet3.title: Two Decades of Master Mentorship
tenet3.text: Conglomerates have automated factories, quarterly investor calls, and overseas assembly lines. This workshop has razor-sharp French gouges, Balkan maple seasoned across generations, and an ear tuned over forty years of devotion. When the bow meets the string, true tone speaks for itself.
tenet3.caption: Mark Edwards (1952–2026) & Matthew Lane

masterQuote.quote: A violin is not a commodity SKU in a corporate distribution center. It is three hundred years of living geometry held under sixty pounds of string tension, waiting for a human hand to awaken its voice. We answer only to the player, the teacher, and the music.
masterQuote.author: Matthew Lane
